summary.en: Analyse schedules and lock cycles, then compare actual MySQL isolation observations.
summary.bn: Schedule ও lock cycle বিশ্লেষণ করো, তারপর MySQL-এর দুই সেশনে isolation-এর ফল দেখো।

notes: InnoDB and enforced CHECK constraints are used; MySQL 8.0.16 or later is required.

sections.title: Let two cashiers work at once
Build a precedence graph before guessing
Move from schedules to actual locks
Avoid false conclusions from one connection

practice.title: Draw a precedence cycle
practice.statementHtml: For r1(X),r2(X),w1(X),w2(X), list conflict edges and decide serialisability.
practice.answerHtml: r1(X) before w2(X) gives T1 → T2. r2(X) before w1(X) gives T2 → T1; w1 before w2 also gives T1 → T2. The two-node cycle means the schedule is not conflict-serialisable.

practice.title: Find a serial order
practice.answerHtml: The X conflicts give T1 → T2. There is no edge back because T1 never accesses Y after T2. The graph is acyclic, so T1 then T2 is an equivalent serial order.

practice.title: Diagnose an account deadlock
practice.statementHtml: A locks account 1 then requests 2; B locks 2 then requests 1. Explain the graph and response.
hints: A wait-for edge points towards the holder.
practice.answerHtml: A waits for B and B waits for A, producing a cycle. InnoDB can choose either victim and roll it back with 1213. Retry the whole victim transaction safely. Using a consistent account-id lock order reduces this cycle.

practice.title: Predict a snapshot experiment
practice.statementHtml: At REPEATABLE READ, A reads 1000, B commits 900, then A repeats an ordinary SELECT. What does A see?
hints: The first consistent read has already established the snapshot.
practice.answerHtml: A sees 1000 under its established consistent-read snapshot, assuming A has not changed the row itself. A new transaction can see 900. A locking read is a different access mode and is not constrained to that old snapshot.

practice.title: Distinguish error boundaries
practice.statementHtml: How should an application handle errors 1213 and 1205 in an atomic transfer?
hints: Statement rollback and transaction rollback differ.
practice.answerHtml: 1213 aborts the deadlock victim transaction, so restart it from the beginning. A 1205 lock timeout normally rolls back only the waiting statement under the default setting; explicitly roll back the whole transfer before retrying. Neither case justifies committing an incomplete transfer.

quiz.prompt: Which operation pair conflicts in a precedence test?
quiz.explanation: At least one write and the same item are required.

quiz.prompt: What does an acyclic precedence graph establish?
options: Absence of every deadlock in the server
quiz.explanation: A topological order supplies an equivalent serial order.

quiz.prompt: Which phase follows the first lock release in basic 2PL?
quiz.explanation: No new lock may be acquired after shrinking starts.

quiz.prompt: Which error identifies an InnoDB deadlock victim?
quiz.explanation: Deadlock detection aborts a selected transaction.

quiz.prompt: At READ COMMITTED, what can a repeated plain SELECT see after another transaction commits?
quiz.explanation: Each consistent read takes a new snapshot.

quiz.prompt: When does ordinary REPEATABLE READ establish its snapshot?
quiz.explanation: An explicit consistent-snapshot request can establish it earlier.

quiz.prompt: What is a SELECT FOR UPDATE intended to acquire?
options: Current data with locks for a later change
Only an old snapshot with no locks
quiz.explanation: The locks protect rows during the active transaction.

quiz.prompt: Does a stable snapshot alone imply general serialisability?
Which graph diagnoses a lock waiting cycle?
quiz.explanation: Edges point from waiting transactions to lock holders.

quiz.prompt: What reduces the two-account opposite-order deadlock pattern?
options: Acquire account locks in a common id order
Keep transactions open during user input
quiz.explanation: A common order prevents that circular acquisition pattern.

quiz.prompt: Can a plain SERIALIZABLE SELECT in an explicit transaction block a writer?
quiz.explanation: InnoDB converts the read to shared locking in this transaction context.

quiz.prompt: Which default timeout behaviour makes an explicit whole-operation rollback important?
options: 1205 can undo only the waiting statement
quiz.explanation: Earlier transfer statements may still be pending.

keyPoints.en: Conflicting operations access one item in different transactions with at least one write.
keyPoints.bn: দুই ট্রানজ্যাকশন একই আইটেমে কাজ করলে আর অন্তত একটি write হলে conflict হয়।

keyPoints.en: An acyclic precedence graph proves conflict serialisability.
keyPoints.bn: Precedence graph এঁকে দেখো, কোনো cycle না থাকলে schedule-টা conflict-serialisable হবে।

keyPoints.en: Two-phase locking separates lock acquisition from lock release.
keyPoints.bn: Two-phase locking-এ lock নেওয়ার পর্ব আর ছাড়ার পর্ব আলাদা থাকে।

keyPoints.en: A deadlock needs victim handling and a safe whole-transaction retry.
keyPoints.bn: Deadlock হলে victim ট্রানজ্যাকশন সামলে পুরো কাজ নিরাপদে আবার চালাতে হয়।

keyPoints.en: InnoDB snapshot reads and locking reads have different visibility rules.
keyPoints.bn: InnoDB-তে snapshot read আর locking read একই নিয়মে ডেটা দেখে না।

keyPoints.en: A repeatable-read snapshot starts with the first consistent read unless explicitly requested earlier.
keyPoints.bn: REPEATABLE READ-এ আলাদা করে snapshot না চাইলে প্রথম consistent read থেকে snapshot শুরু হয়।
